item.title: A plan months in the making and 'a very hard worker' – How Uno-X Mobility grabbed double success at the Tour de France Femmes
item.content:encoded: Uno-X Mobility have a huge amount to celebrate at the Tour de France Femmes on Monday evening, with Sigrid Haugset putting in an enormous ride to secure not only the team's first Tour stage win, but pull on the yellow jersey, too. But this win was far from spontaneous.In fact, Uno-X have had this stage circled for several weeks, and have been down to southeast France with Haugset to recon these roads, so they knew exactly what they wanted to do on stage 3.Attacking more than 80km from the finish and riding solo for over half the stage may not have been the exact way anyone expected her to win, but that knowledge only boosted Haugset's confidence in the finale, which was essential when she had Lotte Kopecky (SD Worx-Protime) chasing her down.Once the emotional celebrations at the bus had calmed down, Haugset's DS and performance director gave their insights into the team's biggest win yet."We just said to stay focused, keep it cool, eat, drink, focus on a good line, and don't give up," Uno-X DS Nicolas Marche said at the finish, explaining what the team car was telling Haugset as Kopecky came within 10 seconds of her."As I say, we knew the course very well, she knew it very well, we came here to recon one or two months ago, so we knew exactly the route so we knew exactly - where it's important to keep energy and to pull. We knew also that Kopecky in this downhill will be faster, also a bit more heavy and stuff. So we kept believing, but it's just incredible."We really just encouraged her to keep going, no matter if Kopecky came up, it looked like yellow, so it was a win-win anyway," performance director Jesper Bundgaard Vinkel added. "So we just pushed her all we could."Though many people may have looked at Kopecky as the strongest rider, her team knew the Norwegian had the strength to win."Sigrid is working so hard every day; she's a special girl, she's not been that long in cycling, so I don't imagine many people really know how strong she is," Bundgaard Vinkel said."I think we put in a lot of hard work, everybody in the team, Sigrid as well, and she's really a fighter. We picked this stage before the start of the Tour, this one and another one, to go full-in, and she did, and it was incredible that it worked out."Their faith didn't falter when Kopecky made inroads, as they felt that Haugset was still stronger where it counted."Actually, Kopecky and Sigrid we saw on the final climb were a bit the same in terms of physical level, and then we had a very technical downhill where we know that Kopecky [is strong]. [Sigrid] almost crashed actually, and she [Kopecky] took time there. We knew that is a big strength of Kopecky, and we knew the final was actually always slightly up and down and really about the physical level, so we kept pushing," Marche explained."At 10 seconds we said 'Now it's you and a TT, and physically you are on the same level as Kopecky so just keep going and keep going to the line and don't give up'. We really believed in it, and she showed it."Haugset isn't a name that all viewers will be familiar with, but those who have been watching carefully will have taken note of her impressive rides in hard races so far this year, with her results sheet probably not quite reflecting how strong she has been."She's just an amazing rider to work with, always happy, always smiling. A very hard worker, I think I never saw a rider working so hard, so dedicated to what she is doing, and I think now she showed to the world who she is," is how Marche described the 27-year-old, who only started racing professionally in 2022."I think she showed it already a little bit this year, her first year in WorldTour; she came from Continental, she developed. This year was a development process with her, we took the time, we don't put pressure, and I think in the Giro we saw what she's capable of. She was there to support, and at the end she had some impressive stages, especially the last stage of the Giro; she was with the best, it was all about physically."So we know what she's able to do, and that's the goal actually, to come to this Tour with Sigrid to actually take an opportunity like today and taking [the win] already today, the first one that we [highlighted], it's just unbelievable, and I think more to come. The Tour is only just starting."Indeed, the Tour is only just starting, and so are Uno-X's ambitions. After achieving their goal of moving their men's team up into the WorldTour – and in fact winning a men's Tour stage in 2025 and wearing the yellow jersey this year – the next goal for the Norwegian team is about pushing their women's programme to the next level. Haugset pulling on yellow on Monday, even if she may not expect to hold it for long, is the next big step in that journey."We have a big goal in the team to win the yellow jersey in the overall in 2030 with the men and women, so I think this summer shows that we are on the way," Bundgaard Vinkel said.Marche was similarly proud: "We are in the process of this goal and dream, but I think we are showing who we are now."Support our unrivalled coverage of the Tour de France Femmes and women's cycling by subscribing to Cyclingnews. item.title: 'We have to do a checkup this evening and see how it goes tomorrow' – Demi Vollering suffers early crash on challenging stage 3 of Tour de France Femmes
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: The Dutch rider fell along with new mountains classification leader Puck Pieterse and world champion Magdeleine Vallieres as the peloton raced up the day's opening climb, just 13km into the race.Vollering avoided serious injury and was quick to get back on her bike. However, after warming down following the stage finish in Poligny, she looked to be walking gingerly after climbing off her time trial bike.Vollering's team refused media requests for both her and her teammate Célia Gery after the stage, which was run through the Jura hills in temperatures reaching 35°C. Team directeur sportif Nicolas Maire was on hand to break down the stage and said that Vollering will undergo further checkups ahead of Tuesday's stage 4 time trial."She looks OK. We'll try to see with the physio how she feels, but we have to do a checkup this evening and see how it goes tomorrow," he told before admitting that he had expected more action from the stage, which saw a group of 37 eventually come together behind phenomenal solo winner Sigrid Haugset and second-placed Lotte Kopecky."We were expecting a bit more from the stage, but I think at one point there is like a poker game, and nobody wants to play for the other, so we lost time," he said, remarking on the time gap to Haugset.The Norwegian launched her astounding attack 89km from the finish line, holding off a charging Kopecky on the road to Poligny. Further back, a larger chase group of GC favourites went clear and then regrouped with those dropped behind as their deficit ballooned to almost three minutes as Vollering and fellow GC contenders Kim Le Court-Pienaar and Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney traded blows over the day's final hills."I would say it's a pity for all the GC contenders, but I just say that Uno-X played well and they deserve the win and the yellow jersey," he added."The Tour is still long, and we'll fight in the next day to come back in the GC, but yeah, we were expecting a bit more from this stage. We tried to be in the breakaway with Célia, but it didn't work exactly as we wanted"I think we missed the move with Kopecky, and that's a bit of a pity if we just look at our race."Maire also said that he expected a bit more work at the front of the chase from Visma-Lease a Bike in particular. The Dutch team had reigning champion Pauline Ferrand-Prévot and Femke de Vries among the lead group, later joined by their sprinter Marianne Vos on the flatter run-in to Poligny."There are a lot of riders like Le Court-Pienaar and Vos who can come here and play for a win, especially without Wiebes. So, I was expecting that they would chase a bit more. Nobody wants to ride for the other, and we arrive at almost three minutes," he said, before turning attention to the time trial, a 21km test against the clock to Dijon."I would say I expect a good TT from Demi, but we know that, for example, normally she will lose time on Reusser, on maybe Van der Breggen," he concluded."Normally, she can win some seconds on some GC contenders, so that's what we are looking for. If she plays really well, I think she can for sure try to be on the podium on this stage."Support our unrivalled coverage of the Tour de France Femmes and women's cycling by subscribing to .
